request.spec:
Closing or soft-closing a period now fixes every person's carried figure for it, as it fixes
their period figures, and reopening makes them live again. And while an as-of date is set, the
consolidated figures over the tree are shown as of that date too: every sheet of the tree as it
stood at the end of that day, with that date as the sheet's today.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Closing or soft-closing a period now fixes every person's carried figure for it, as it fixes
their period figures, and reopening makes them live again. And while an as-of date is set, the
consolidated figures over the tree are shown as of that date too: every sheet of the tree as it
stood at the end of that day, with that date as the sheet's today.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The change is in. Three of the four tests in the spec pass; scenario 2 still fails because of an error in the spec itself, which I'm not allowed to edit.

**Why scenario 2 fails:** at lines 730 and 814 it expects `sheet-parent` to show the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`. That looks like a placeholder that was never filled in: everywhere else the spec uses `` `${sheet}-p` ``, and the app correctly shows the real id (e.g. `smvkkkr2dxo9t-p`). I ran a temporary copy of the spec with only those two lines corrected, and all four scenarios passed, including the rest of scenario 2. Then I deleted the copy. If someone changes those two lines to `` `${sheet}-p` ``, the spec should pass as written.

**What changed:**
- **Carried figures are fixed on close:** when a period is closed, soft-closed, or auto-closed, the server now saves each person's carried figure alongside their period figure. It uses the same rule the screen uses for the live figure. Reopening deletes the saved figures, so they go live again. A person added after the close shows 0.00.
  - A new migration, `V90__period_person_carried.sql`, adds a `carried` column to the current figures and to the period history, so as-of views show the frozen carried figure too.
  - `PeriodCloser`, `PeriodRepository`, `PeriodResponse` and the two period read endpoints handle the new figures. Merging two people adds up their carried figures, as it already did for period figures.
  - On the front end, `personPeriodCarried` in `features/periods/periods.ts` shows the saved figure while a period is closed or soft-closed.
- **Consolidated figures follow the as-of date:** while an as-of date is set, `features/consolidated/consolidated.slot.tsx` reads every sheet in the tree as it stood at the end of that day, with that date as the sheet's today. Which sheets belong to the tree is still worked out from the current parent links, because the app doesn't keep a history of them.

**One change outside the request:** scenario 3 needs a claim dated 2026-02-25 to be reassignable while period 2026-02 is closed. Reassigning one claim was the only closed-period check that also looked at the claim's date; all the others, including bulk reassign, look only at its due-by. I changed `RefuseClosedClaimMove` to check due-by only and updated the comment in `reassign.PUT.yml` to match.

**Port 3002 is taken:** `PORT` is set to 3002 in this environment, and something else is already listening there. A plain `bin/e2e` sends the tests to that other app, and nearly everything fails. I ran with `PORT=3917 bin/e2e`.
